clauses.reason: The order exempts Ashton C. Barrett, a member of the Federal Maritime Commission, from mandatory retirement for age under subsection (c) of section 8335 of title 5 of the United States Code until October 31, 1977. The order recites that he would become subject to mandatory retirement because of age and service as of October 31, 1976. The order is a single command with one fixed term, so its own stated date is the first end: 1977-10-31, recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is 1977-10-30. The order was signed 1976-10-22. No amendment, revocation or shortening of this order is held (searched below).

research_rationale:
EO 11942 (signed 1976-10-22) is a one-person exemption under section 8335(c) of title 5, United States Code: Ashton C. Barrett, a member of the Federal Maritime Commission, is exempted from mandatory retirement for age until October 31, 1977. The held Federal Register text of the order was read in full and is a single operative clause (the recital, the finding of public interest, and the exempting sentence). The order ends by its own terms on 1977-10-31 (inclusive; exclusive alternative 1977-10-30, owner ruling 2026-10-21 on until dates). Searches judged adequate: U.S. Code and eCFR (no hit naming the order), the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note catalog, and the held-text search for the person's full name, which found the chain members recorded above and nothing else. Whether the person left office on or before the stated date is not in any held source and is not asserted.

savings.reason: The exemption only suspended compulsory retirement for the stated term; it creates no continuing duty, office or rule. The person's service during the term and the pay for it had accrued by 1977-10-31; nothing in the order survives that date, and any later exemption is a separate grant recorded as a later event.
